reason: Every finite H needs one exponent uniform in epsilon and all H-free G; a restricted-family argument cannot establish this Erdős–Hajnal-strength assertion. No full-scope route.
source_name: Tung Nguyen, Alex Scott and Paul Seymour, “Induced subgraph density. VII. The five-vertex path”, arXiv:2312.15333 (2026).
statement:
Let $H$ be a finite graph. For $varepsilon\in(0,1/2)$, a graph is **$varepsilon$-restricted** if it or its complement has maximum degree at most $varepsilon$ times its number of vertices. A graph $H$ has the **polynomial Rödl property** if there exists $d>0$ such that every $H$-free graph $G$ has an $varepsilon$-restricted induced subgraph with at least $varepsilon^d|V(G)|$ vertices for every $varepsilon\in(0,1/2)$.

**Fox–Sudakov conjecture.** Every graph $H$ has the polynomial Rödl property.

Rödl's theorem guarantees a positive proportion depending on $varepsilon$, while the conjecture asks for a polynomial dependence. The paper notes that the polynomial Rödl property implies the Erdős–Hajnal property; the conjecture remains open in general.
title: Fox–Sudakov conjecture on the polynomial Rödl property

reason: Linear correction must work for every expander and inner code down to delta*d0>1; distance alone does not give a linear-time decoder. No algorithm with a proved progress invariant.
source_name: Kuan Cheng, Minghui Ouyang, Chong Shangguan and Yuanting Shen, “When can an expander code correct Ω(n) errors in O(n) time?”, arXiv:2312.16087 (2024).
statement: Let $G$ be a $(c,d,\alpha,\delta)$-bipartite expander and let $C_0\subseteq\mathbb{F}_2^d$ be an inner code with minimum Hamming distance $d(C_0)\ge d_0$. Let $T(G,C_0)\subseteq\mathbb{F}_2^n$ denote the associated expander code. **Expander-code trade-off conjecture.** If $\delta d_0>1$, then $T(G,C_0)$ can correct $\Omega_{c,d,\alpha,\delta}(n)$ errors in $O_{c,d,\alpha,\delta}(n)$ time for every such $G$ and $C_0$. This conjecture would make the necessary condition $\delta d_0>1$ essentially sufficient, improving the paper's sufficient condition $\delta d_0>3$ and identifying the fundamental trade-off between expansion and inner-code distance.
title: The fundamental trade-off conjecture for expander-code decoding

reason: All large n and matching sizes s require the exact extremal classification, with construction H² undefined locally. Small matching tests would give no uniform classification.
source_name: Yan Wang and Yi Zhang, “Vertex degree sums for perfect matchings in 3-uniform hypergraphs”, arXiv:2401.03713 (2024).
statement:
Let $H$ be a 3-graph of order $n$, let $sigma_2(H)$ be the minimum of $deg(u)+deg(v)$ over adjacent vertices $u,v$, and let $H_{n,s}^2$ be the corresponding extremal 3-graph. **Zhang–Lu matching extremal conjecture.** There exists $n_0\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, for every 3-graph $H$ of order $n\ge n_0$ without isolated vertices, if

$$
\sigma_2(H)>2\left(\binom{n-1}{2}-\binom{n-s}{2}\right)
$$

and $n\ge3s$, then $H$ contains no matching of size $s$ if and only if $H$ is a subgraph of $H_{n,s}^2$. This extends the stated extremal matching result for the relevant degree-sum threshold; the supplied source gives no resolution of the conjecture.
title: Zhang–Lu matching extremal conjecture for 3-uniform hypergraphs

reason: Perfect-matching threshold depends on an undefined two-parameter construction; divisibility of n and the exact source domain need checking. No full-scope route; wording fixes uncredited.
source_name: Yan Wang and Yi Zhang, “Vertex degree sums for perfect matchings in 3-uniform hypergraphs”, arXiv:2401.03713 (2024).
statement:
Let $H$ be a 3-graph of order $n$, let $sigma_2(H)$ denote the minimum $deg(u)+deg(v)$ over adjacent vertices $u,v$, and let $H^{1,2}_{n,x,y}$ be the construction defined in the source for parameters $x,y$. **Extremal perfect-matching conjecture.** There exists $n_0\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, for every 3-graph $H$ of order $n\ge n_0$ without isolated vertices, if

$$
\sigma_2(H)>\max\left\{\sigma_2(H^{1,2}_{n,x,y}):0\le x,y\le\frac n3-1,\ x+y\le\frac n3-1\right\},
$$

then $H$ contains no perfect matching if and only if $H$ is a subgraph of $H_{n,n/3}^2$. The source explains that an earlier conjecture fails when $s=n/3$ and near that range, motivating this strengthened extremal formulation; its resolution is not supplied.
title: Conjecture on the extremal obstruction to perfect matchings

reason: Threshold must depend only on maximum degree despite arbitrary order of F, with g allowed to depend on F. No bounded-degree uniform subdivision mechanism.
source_name: Lucas Picasarri-Arrieta and Clément Rambaud, “Subdivisions in dicritical digraphs with large order or digirth”, arXiv:2401.05938 (2024).
statement:
Let $F$ be a digraph with maximum degree $\Delta$. For an integer $g$, let $\mathrm{mader}_{\vec{\chi}}^{(g)}(F)$ be the least integer $k$, if it exists, such that every digraph $D$ with dichromatic number $\vec{\chi}(D)\geq k$ and digirth at least $g$ contains a subdivision of $F$. **Large-digirth dichromatic subdivision conjecture.** There is a function $f$ such that, for every digraph $F$ with maximum degree $\Delta$, there is an integer $g$ satisfying

$$
\mathrm{mader}_{\vec{\chi}}^{(g)}(F)\leq f(\Delta).
$$

This asserts that sufficiently large digirth permits a subdivision threshold controlled only by the maximum degree. The source says that this bound is believed to hold, but gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
title: Large-digirth dichromatic subdivision bound by maximum degree

primary_review.assessment: Conjecture 1.6 literal weighted statement confirmed. Lemma 2.2 probability proof and Corollary 2.3 read. Source later ties bridgeless case to weighted perfect matchings; no full all-graph route. Isolate shortcut fails by exact enumeration.

reason: Weighted bisection invites a tiny certificate, but disconnected extensions of the excluded claw may only expose an omitted source hypothesis. Inspect source before treating such a witness as substantive.
source_name: Stefanie Gerke, Gregory Gutin, Anders Yeo and Yacong Zhou, “Lower Bounds for Maximum Weight Bisections of Graphs with Bounded Degrees”, arXiv:2401.10074 (2024).
statement:
Let $G=(V,E,w)$ be a weighted triangle-free subcubic graph, meaning that $G$ has no triangle and maximum degree at most $3$, with non-negative edge weights and total edge weight $w(G)$. A **bisection** is a cut whose two parts differ in size by at most $1$.

**Triangle-free subcubic bisection conjecture.** Every weighted triangle-free subcubic graph other than $K_{1,3}$ has a bisection of weight at least

$$
\frac{11}{15}w(G).
$$

The paper proves a lower bound of $\frac{613}{855}w(G)$ for graphs other than $K_{1,3}$ and notes that the Petersen graph may make $\frac{11}{15}$ optimal; the conjectured improvement remains open.
title: Weighted triangle-free subcubic bisection conjecture

reason: Finite computational ranges cannot classify all distance sets of arbitrary cardinality and magnitudes. No bounded certificate or structural characterization found.
source_name: Janka Oravcová and Roman Soták, “On a problem concerning integer distance graphs”, arXiv:2401.12347 (2024).
statement:
Let $D\subseteq\mathbb N$ be a distance set, let $G(D)$ be its integer distance graph, let $\chi(D)$ be its chromatic number, and let $\omega(G(D))$ be the clique number of $G(D)$. Assume

$$
\operatorname{gcd}(D)=1
$$

and $\chi(D)=|D|+1$. **The maximum-chromatic distance graph conjecture.** Then one of the following holds:

$$
D=\{1,4,5,6,7\},\qquad D=\{1,2,3,\dots,2k-1,2k+1,4k\},\qquad \text{or}\qquad \omega(G(D))\geq |D|.
$$

The claim is motivated by the question of determining all integer distance graphs whose chromatic number attains the general upper bound $|D|+1$. The source reports computational verification for distance sets with $4\leq |D|\leq 11$ in specified ranges, but gives no proof or resolution of the general assertion.
title: Characterization of maximum-chromatic integer distance graphs

reason: Labeling invariant requires source definition and possible connectedness/size exceptions. Arbitrary-graph two-value labeling has no supplied construction; isolated-vertex wording issues earn no credit.
source_name: G. C. Lau, “Complete characterization of graphs with local total antimagic chromatic number 3”, arXiv:2401.14653 (2024).
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $k$ pendant edges, let $\Delta(G)$ be its maximum degree, and let $\chi_{lt}(G)$ denote its local total antimagic chromatic number. **Local total antimagic bound conjecture.** If $k\leq\Delta(G)$, then

$$
\Delta(G)+1\leq\chi_{lt}(G)\leq\Delta(G)+2.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the known results summarized in the paper; whether these bounds hold for every such graph remains open.
title: The local total antimagic bound for graphs with few pendant edges

reason: Mixed-boundary eigenfunction maximum needs geometry-dependent PDE control over every triangle. Ambiguity about first positive nontrivial eigenfunction requires source fidelity; no short full route.
source_name: Rui Li and Ruofei Yao, “Monotonicity of positive solutions to semilinear elliptic equations with mixed boundary conditions in triangles”, arXiv:2401.17912 (2026).
statement: Let $T$ be a triangle with mixed boundary conditions: Neumann conditions on two sides and a Dirichlet condition on the remaining side. Consider the first positive non-trivial eigenfunction of the corresponding mixed Laplacian problem. **Hot spots conjecture for mixed triangles.** Its maximum occurs at the corner opposite to the Dirichlet side. This question is part of the 2012 Polymath project on the hot spots conjecture. The surrounding linear problem has since seen substantial progress, but the source presents this specific mixed-boundary question without stating a resolution.
title: The hot spots conjecture for mixed eigenfunctions in triangles

reason: Pascal recurrence needs a dimension-reduction injection controlling overlaps for all k,d; boundary cases do not give it. Endpoint n(k,d-1) also needs conventions.
source_name: Jarosław Grytczuk, Andrzej P. Kisielewicz and Krzysztof Przesławski, “Neighborly boxes and bipartite coverings; constructions and conjectures”, arXiv:2402.02199 (2024).
statement:
Let $n(0,d)=1$ for all $d\geqslant1$, and for $1\leqslant k\leqslant d$ let $n(k,d)$ be the maximum number of pairwise $k$-neighborly boxes in $\mathbb{R}^d$. **Pascal-type conjecture.** For every $1\leqslant k\leqslant d$,

$$
n(k,d)\leqslant n(k-1,d-1)+n(k,d-1).
$$

The conjecture is known in the cases $k=1$, $k=d$, and $k=d-1$; in general it would imply the limit conjecture with $\gamma_k=1/k!$.
title: Alon–Grynkiewicz–Kisielewicz–Przesławski Pascal-type conjecture for neighborly boxes

reason: Splitting produces hierarchical codes, while optimal arbitrary codes need not be hierarchical. No universal transformation preserving cardinality and k-neighborliness; finite search not pursued.
source_name: Jarosław Grytczuk, Andrzej P. Kisielewicz and Krzysztof Przesławski, “Neighborly boxes and bipartite coverings; constructions and conjectures”, arXiv:2402.02199 (2024).
statement:
Let $S^d$ be the set of strings of length $d$ over $\{0,1,*\}$. A splitting replaces one joker in a string by $0$ and $1$; a splitting is legal when replacing the original string preserves the property of being a $k$-neighborly code. Let $\operatorname{score}(k,d)$ be the maximum size of a $k$-neighborly code obtainable by legal splittings starting from the all-jokers string, and let $n(k,d)$ be the maximum size of any $k$-neighborly code in $S^d$. **Splitting-game optimality conjecture.** There exists a strategy in the splitting game resulting in a $k$-neighborly code of maximum size, that is,

$$
\operatorname{score}(k,d)=n(k,d),
$$

for every $1\leqslant k\leqslant d$. This asks whether optimal neighborly codes can always be constructed through the splitting game.
title: Splitting-game optimality conjecture for neighborly codes

reason: Asymptotic error is smaller than the central binomial coefficient for every bipartite G. Neither the poset encoding nor a matching construction is supplied locally; no full route.
source_name: Dániel Gerbner and Balázs Patkós, “A note on vertex Turán problems in the Kneser cube”, arXiv:2402.02525 (2024).
statement:
Let $G$ be a bipartite graph that is not a matching. For a poset $P$, let $\mathop{}\!\mathrm{La}_{sym}(n,P)$ denote the maximum size of a $P$-free complement-closed family of subsets of $[n]$, and let $P_{G,A}$ be the poset associated with the part $A$ of $G$. **The complement-closed Lubell bound conjecture.**

$$
\mathop{}\!\mathrm{vex}(n,G)=2^{n-1}+\frac{1}{2}\mathop{}\!\mathrm{La}_{sym}(n,P_{G,A})+o\left(\binom{n}{n/2}\right).
$$

This conjecture asserts that the complement-closed poset-free-family upper bound gives the correct asymptotics for every bipartite graph that is not a matching. The source provides no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
title: The complement-closed Lubell bound conjecture for bipartite graphs

reason: Continuity in integer exponents is vacuous without a specified continuous interpolation; largest t for all m,s versus for fixed m,s is ambiguous. Correcting this is not a discovery.
source_name: Jared J. L. Brannan, Benjamin J. Clark and Garrett J. Kepler, “Properties of the cone of polynomials of fixed degree that preserve nonnegative matrices”, arXiv:2402.04508 (2024).
statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}_n$ be the set of polynomials preserving nonnegative matrices of order $n$. For $m,s\in\mathbb{Z}^{\geq 0}$ with $s>m\geq n$, define

$$
p_t(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}x^k-tx^m+\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}x^{s+k}.
$$

**Continuity conjecture.** The largest $t\in\mathbb{R}^+$ such that $p_t\in\mathcal{P}_n$ for all such $m,s$ is a continuous function of $m$ and $s$, bounded between $1$ and $2$. The claim proposes a precise description of how the optimal coefficient bound varies with the exponents.
title: The continuity conjecture for the optimal negative coefficient bound

reason: Maximal packing gives the known Delta*rho scale, but obtaining a connectedness saving of rho-1 requires an additional global exchange argument. No such invariant; do not repackage the weaker bound.
source_name: Renzo Gómez and Juan Gutiérrez, “Domination and packing in graphs”, arXiv:2402.05088 (2024).
statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph with at least two vertices. Write $\gamma(G)$ for its domination number, $\rho(G)$ for its packing number, and $\Delta$ for its maximum degree.

**Domination-packing conjecture.** For every such graph,

$$
\gamma(G) \leq (\Delta-1)\rho(G)+1.
$$

The paper presents this as a stronger version of the previously stated conjecture, following the known bound $\gamma(G)\leq\Delta\rho(G)$ for graphs without isolated vertices. The authors state that their techniques are still far from settling this conjecture.
title: Domination-packing conjecture for connected graphs

reason: Needs a high-probability comparison of longest cycle and largest proper subsystem in a uniform Steiner model. No distributional control; finitely many systems cannot settle the limit.
source_name: Michael J. Gill, Adam Mammoliti and Ian M. Wanless, “Canonical labelling of Latin squares in average-case polynomial time”, arXiv:2402.06205 (2024).
statement:
Let $S$ be a Steiner quasigroup of order $n$ selected uniformly at random. Let $\ell(S)$ be the length of its longest row cycle, and let $m(S)$ be the size of its largest proper Steiner subsystem. **Random Steiner quasigroup conjecture.** With probability $1-o(1)$,

$$
\ell(S)>m(S).
$$

If true, this structural property would yield average-case polynomial-time canonical labelling, and hence isomorphism testing, for Steiner triple systems. The source presents it as a belief and gives no evidence of a resolution, so it remains open.
title: Random Steiner quasigroup row-cycle and subsystem conjecture

reason: Uniform random factorisation has dependent row cycles and subsystems. No full high-probability estimate or constructive certificate route.
source_name: Michael J. Gill, Adam Mammoliti and Ian M. Wanless, “Canonical labelling of Latin squares in average-case polynomial time”, arXiv:2402.06205 (2024).
statement:
Let $\mathcal{U}$ be the Latin square representing a uniformly random 1-factorisation of $K_{2n}$. Let $\ell(\mathcal{U})$ be the length of its longest row cycle, and let $s(\mathcal{U})$ be the size of its largest proper sub-1-factorisation. **Random 1-factorisation conjecture.** With probability $1-o(1)$,

$$
\ell(\mathcal{U})>s(\mathcal{U}).
$$

If true, this analogue of the proposed Steiner-quasigroup property would imply average-case polynomial-time canonical labelling for these 1-factorisations. The source gives no evidence of a resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
title: Random 1-factorisation substructure conjecture

reason: Existence of a Hamilton row cycle in almost every Latin square is a random-structure statement, not a single example. No tractable proof route.
source_name: Michael J. Gill, Adam Mammoliti and Ian M. Wanless, “Canonical labelling of Latin squares in average-case polynomial time”, arXiv:2402.06205 (2024).
statement:
Let $L$ be a Latin square of order $n$, and let $\ell(L)$ denote the length of its longest row cycle. **Longest row-cycle conjecture.** As $n\to\infty$, asymptotically almost all Latin squares of order $n$ satisfy

$$
\ell(L)=n.
$$

This conjecture is based on numerical evidence and asserts that a uniformly typical Latin square has a row cycle of maximum possible length. The source gives no resolution, so it remains open.
title: Longest row-cycle conjecture for random Latin squares

reason: Constant spectral ratio uniformly in n needs global Hamiltonicity machinery; fixed density or growing ratio results do not cover it. No new mechanism and no current-body status clearance.
source_name: Nemanja Draganić, Richard Montgomery, David Munhá Correia, Alexey Pokrovskiy and Benny Sudakov, “Hamiltonicity of expanders: optimal bounds and applications”, arXiv:2402.06603 (2024).
statement:
Let $G$ be an $(n,d,\lambda)$-graph, meaning a $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices whose second-largest eigenvalue in absolute value satisfies $|\lambda(G)|\leq\lambda$.

**Krivelevich–Sudakov conjecture.** There exists $C>0$ such that if

$$
\frac{d}{\lambda}\geq C,
$$

then every $(n,d,\lambda)$-graph is Hamiltonian.

This conjecture seeks a constant spectral-expansion condition guaranteeing Hamiltonicity, strengthening the previously known bound depending on $n$. It is known in the case $d\geq n^\alpha$ for every fixed $\alpha$, but remains open in general.
title: Krivelevich–Sudakov conjecture on Hamiltonicity of pseudorandom graphs

reason: Polynomial lower-bound conjectures conflict in order with next row's linear claim for the same posets. Must resolve source chronology and bodies; no inference from metadata.
source_name: Dingyuan Liu, “Induced saturation for complete bipartite posets”, arXiv:2402.08651 (2026).
statement:
For $s\geq 2$, let $\mathcal{K}_{s,t}$ be the complete bipartite poset with $s$ upper-layer and $t$ lower-layer pairwise incomparable vertices, every upper-layer vertex larger than every lower-layer vertex. Let $\mathrm{sat}^{*}(n,\mathcal{K}_{s,t})$ denote the smallest size of an induced $\mathcal{K}_{s,t}$-saturated family in $2^{[n]}$. **Ivan's conjecture.** For all $s\geq 2$,

$$
\mathrm{sat}^{*}(n,\mathcal{K}_{s,2})=\Theta(n^{s})\quad\text{and}\quad\mathrm{sat}^{*}(n,\mathcal{K}_{s,s})=\Theta(n^{2s-2}).
$$

The source notes that the corresponding upper bounds were proved, while the conjecture asks for matching lower bounds and strengthens the earlier $\mathcal{K}_{2,2}$ conjecture.
title: Ivan's complete bipartite poset saturation conjecture

reason: Source text reports t=2 determined linear, which would defeat part of previous row if definitions agree. General fixed s,t lower bound still not proved here; primary-body HOLD.
source_name: Dingyuan Liu, “Induced saturation for complete bipartite posets”, arXiv:2402.08651 (2026).
statement:
Let $s\geq t\geq 2$ be fixed, and let $\mathcal{K}_{s,t}$ be the complete bipartite poset with $s$ upper-layer and $t$ lower-layer pairwise incomparable vertices, every upper-layer vertex larger than every lower-layer vertex. Let $\mathrm{sat}^{*}(n,\mathcal{K}_{s,t})$ denote the smallest size of an induced $\mathcal{K}_{s,t}$-saturated family in $2^{[n]}$. **The linear-order conjecture.**

$$
\mathrm{sat}^{*}(n,\mathcal{K}_{s,t})=\Theta(n)
$$

for all fixed $s\geq t\geq 2$. The conjecture proposes that the upper bound proved earlier in the paper is tight up to a multiplicative constant, extending the determined linear order for the $t=2$ case.
title: Linear-order conjecture for complete bipartite poset saturation

reason: For k>2 and growing Delta, independent list assignment still creates correlated obstructions. No uniform union bound meeting both scales established; k=2 excluded as a parameter instance.
source_name: Dan Hefetz and Michael Krivelevich, “Colouring graphs from random lists”, arXiv:2402.09998 (2024).
statement: Given positive integers $k \leq m$, a random $(k,m)$-list-assignment assigns independently to each vertex a uniformly random $k$-element subset of $\{1,\ldots,m\}$. An $n$-vertex graph is **$(k,m)$-colourable** when it has a proper colouring choosing the colour of every vertex from its assigned list. Let $k \geq 2$ be fixed, and let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph with maximum degree $\Delta:= \Delta(n)$. **Casselgren's conjecture.** If $m \gg n^{1/k^2}\Delta^{1/k}$ and $m \gg \Delta$, then $G$ is asymptotically almost surely $(k,m)$-colourable. This extends the known threshold for bounded-degree graphs to graphs whose maximum degree may grow with $n$; the case $k=2$ is known, as is the bounded-degree case, while the general conjecture remains open.
title: Casselgren's random-list colouring conjecture for graphs of unbounded degree

reason: All hypergraphs on fewer than twenty vertices is an enormous unconstrained game-class search. Arbitrary edge subsets and distinct game rules need source definitions; no small exhaustive certificate route.
source_name: Peter Danziger, Melissa A. Huggan, Rehan Malik and Trent G. Marbach, “Tic-Tac-Toe on Designs”, arXiv:2402.11118 (2024).
statement: A **hypergraph** is a pair consisting of a vertex set and a collection of subsets of that vertex set, called hyperedges. In the Tic-Tac-Toe game on a hypergraph, Maker wins if Maker can occupy a hyperedge, while Ophelia can force a draw if she can prevent either player from occupying a hyperedge. **Minimum-order conjecture.** Any hypergraph that is Maker win and where Ophelia can force a draw must have at least $20$ vertices. The conjecture is motivated by the verified example on the transversal design $\mathrm{TD}(4,5)$, which has $20$ vertices and is both Maker win and Ophelia draw; the preceding discussion reports no smaller example, but does not establish the lower bound.
title: Minimum-order conjecture for Maker-win hypergraphs with Ophelia draws

primary_review.assessment: Conjecture 7.1 confirms the full weighted quantifiers. Lemma 3.2 proof solves singleton forbidden set only; symmetric exchange cannot prevent landing in a different forbidden label for larger F. No valid all-F extension.

reason: Weighted optimum must be achieved within |F| exchanges of every chosen minimum basis, not merely some avoiding basis. Ordinary exchange does not preserve this optimality constraint; inspect source before investing.
source_name: Florian Hörsch, András Imolay, Ryuhei Mizutani, Taihei Oki and Tamás Schwarcz, “Problems on Group-labeled Matroid Bases”, arXiv:2402.16259 (2024).
statement: Let $M$ be a matroid on a ground set $E$, let $\Gamma$ be an abelian group, let $\psi\colon E\to\Gamma$ be a group labeling, let $F\subseteq\Gamma$ be a finite set, and let $w\colon E\to\mathbb{R}$ be a weight function. An **$F$-avoiding basis** is a basis whose label is not in $F$. **Weighted bounded-exchange conjecture.** If $M$ has an $F$-avoiding basis, then for every minimum-weight basis $B$, there is a minimum-weight $F$-avoiding basis $B^*$ such that $|B\setminus B^*|\leq |F|$. This stronger weighted analogue is posed as an open problem alongside the unweighted conjectures.
title: The weighted bounded-exchange conjecture for F-avoiding matroid bases

reason: Uniform positive constant over arbitrary digraphs is far stronger than regular-digraph bounds. Girth of acyclic graphs and path conventions need source domain; no full route.
source_name: Yangyang Cheng and Peter Keevash, “On the length of directed paths in digraphs”, arXiv:2402.16776 (2024).
statement:
For a digraph $D$, let $ell(D)$ be the length of a longest directed path, let $g(D)$ be its girth, and let $delta^+(D)$ be its minimum out-degree. **Proposed weaker Thomassé conjecture.** There is some constant $c>0$ such that

$$
\ell(D) \ge c\,g(D)\,\delta^+(D)
$$

for every digraph $D$.

This conjecture weakens Thomassé's proposed bound and is motivated by the paper's lower bounds for regular digraphs. The supplied text does not state whether it is known or remains open, so its database status is left open.
title: A linear lower bound for directed-path length in terms of girth and minimum out-degree

reason: Literal statement already attributes a proof to its own source. Source-body confirmation needed before definitive retirement; no discovery eligibility from reproving refined absorption.
source_name: Michelle Delcourt and Luke Postle, “Proof of the High Girth Existence Conjecture via Refined Absorption”, arXiv:2402.17856 (2024).
statement:
A **Steiner system** with parameters $(n,q,r)$ is a design in which every $r$-subset belongs to exactly one $q$-subset. For a partial $(n,q,r)$-Steiner system, the **girth** is the smallest integer $g\geq2$ for which it has a $((q-r)g+r,g)$-configuration. **High-girth existence conjecture.** For all integers $q > r \geq 2$ and every integer $g\ge 2$, there exists $n_0$ such that for all $n\ge n_0$ satisfying

$$
\binom{q-i}{r-i}~|~\binom{n-i}{r-i}
$$

for all $0\le i \le r-1$, there exists an $(n,q,r)$-Steiner system with girth at least $g$. This is presented as a common generalization of the design Existence Conjecture and Erdős' high-girth Steiner triple-system conjecture. The paper's title and abstract state that it proves this conjecture via refined absorption.
title: The high-girth existence conjecture for Steiner systems

reason: Universal forbidden oriented H and polynomial dichromatic saving would need a major structural mechanism. No acyclic-set extraction controlling the colouring quantifier.
source_name: Pierre Aboulker, Frédéric Havet, François Pirot and Juliette Schabanel, “Minimum acyclic number and maximum dichromatic number of oriented triangle-free graphs of a given order”, arXiv:2403.02298 (2024).
statement:
Let $H$ be an oriented graph, and let an **$H$-free** oriented graph be one that does not contain $H$ as a not necessarily induced subdigraph. For an oriented graph $D$, write $\vec\alpha(D)$ for its maximum acyclic set size and $\vec\chi(D)$ for its dichromatic number. **Harutyunyan–McDiarmid conjecture.** For every oriented graph $H$, there is $\epsilon>0$ such that every $H$-free oriented graph $D$ of order $n$ satisfies

$$
\vec\alpha(D)\geq n^\epsilon\qquad\text{and}\qquad \vec\chi(D)\leq n^{1-\epsilon}.
$$

This conjecture is open even when $H$ is the directed cycle of length $3$, and it strengthens the Alon–Pachs–Solymosi conjecture below.
title: Harutyunyan–McDiarmid conjecture on acyclic sets in H-free oriented graphs

reason: All forbidden tournaments is Erdős–Hajnal scale; special H cases cannot establish the universal quantifier. No small full-scope route.
source_name: Pierre Aboulker, Frédéric Havet, François Pirot and Juliette Schabanel, “Minimum acyclic number and maximum dichromatic number of oriented triangle-free graphs of a given order”, arXiv:2403.02298 (2024).
statement:
Let $H$ be a tournament. An **$H$-free** tournament is one that does not contain $H$ as a not necessarily induced subdigraph. For a tournament $T$, write $\vec\alpha(T)$ for its maximum acyclic set size. **Alon–Pachs–Solymosi conjecture.** For every tournament $H$, there exists $\epsilon>0$ such that every $H$-free tournament $T$ of order $n$ satisfies

$$
\vec\alpha(T)\geq n^\epsilon.
$$

This conjecture is equivalent to the Erdős–Hajnal conjecture. It is known for a few types of tournaments $H$, but remains wide open in general.
title: Alon–Pachs–Solymosi conjecture on acyclic sets in H-free tournaments

reason: Finiteness for every fixed ell and all sufficiently large k needs disjoint directed cycles with distinct lengths; one-cycle bounds do not supply disjointness. No constructive threshold.
source_name: Yandong Bai and Wenpei Jia, “Vertex-disjoint cycles of different lengths in tournaments”, arXiv:2403.03692 (2024).
statement:
Let $h(k,\ell)$ be the source's minimum-outdegree threshold for forcing $k$ vertex-disjoint directed cycles with $\ell$ different lengths. **Weak finiteness conjecture.** For every positive integer $\ell$, if the positive integer $k$ is sufficiently large compared with $\ell$, then

$$
h(k,\ell)\text{ is finite}.
$$

This is proposed as a weaker alternative to Lichiardopol's conjecture on the finiteness of $h(k,k)$. The source gives no resolution and presents the statement for further research.
title: Weak finiteness conjecture for prescribed numbers of different cycle lengths

reason: Global measurable optimum cannot follow from verifying the given non-KS valuation. No upper-bound dual certificate or improved positive-measure construction.
source_name: Tom Williams and Andrei Constantin, “Maximal Non-Kochen-Specker Sets and a Lower Bound on the Size of Kochen-Specker Sets”, arXiv:2403.05230 (2025).
statement: Let a non-Kochen–Specker set in dimension $d$ be a measurable subset $A\subseteq S^{d-1}$ admitting a valuation map $v:A\to\{0,1\}$ such that $v(-n)=v(n)$, every mutually orthogonal collection has valuation sum at most $1$, and every set of $d$ mutually orthogonal directions has valuation sum $1$. In the construction discussed, $N=N_0\cup N_1\subseteq S^2$ is a non-Kochen–Specker set, with normalized measure $|N|=2-\sqrt{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}\ln 2}{\pi}\approx0.8978$. **Maximal non-Kochen–Specker set conjecture.** $N$ is the non-Kochen–Specker set of largest measure. The preceding calculation establishes only the lower bound $|N_{\mathrm{max}}|\geq 2-\sqrt{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}\ln 2}{\pi}\approx0.8978$; whether this particular set is globally maximal is not resolved in the supplied context.
title: Maximal non-Kochen–Specker set conjecture

reason: Every bipartite H needs an n-uniform comparison to ex(n,H), with unrestricted f_H(t). Standard KST upper bounds need not match ex(n,H); no valid bridge supplied.
source_name: Xiying Du and Rose McCarty, “A survey of degree-boundedness”, arXiv:2403.05737 (2024).
statement:
For a graph $H$ and an integer $n$, let $\operatorname{ex}(n,H)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph with no subgraph isomorphic to $H$. **Hereditary Kővári–Sós–Turán conjecture.** For each bipartite graph $H$, there is a function $f_H$ such that every $n$-vertex graph with no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$ and no subgraph isomorphic to $K_{t,t}$ has at most

$$
f_H(t)\operatorname{ex}(n,H)
$$

edges.

This conjecture asks for an extremal bound relative to the ordinary $H$-extremal number, while allowing arbitrary dependence on $t$. It is presented as an open problem connected to efficient degree-bounds.
title: Hunter–Milojević–Sudakov–Tomon hereditary Kővári–Sós–Turán conjecture

primary_review.assessment: Definition 9.1 and Conjecture 9.2 read with full positivity-to-greedy-partition proof. This exact route is already in the source; positivity of all q-Catalan germs is the unresolved bridge. Source reports a<=20 tests; repeating them would not resolve unbounded a.

reason: Finite c range still grows with unbounded a, and tilted height/box require exact definitions. A small-a partition is a helper, not the full standard-partition mechanism.
source_name: Drew Armstrong, “Lattice Points and Rational q-Catalan Numbers”, arXiv:2403.06318 (2026).
statement:
Let $\mathcal{L}=\mathbb{Z}^{a-1}$, let $\operatorname{Box}$ be the fundamental box, and for coprime $a,c$ let $c'$ be the largest integer less than $c$ with $\gcd(a,c')=1$. A standard set is a set of lattice points whose tilted-height generating function is a monomial times $[a]_q$. **Standard-partition conjecture.** For every integer $c$ with $1\leq c\leq(a-1)^2$ and $\gcd(a,c)=1$, the set

$$
\mathcal{L}\cap\operatorname{Box}[c'+1,c]
$$

has a standard partition. Such partitions would support the positivity and lattice interpretation of q-Catalan germs; the source leaves the assertion as a conjecture.
title: Standard-partition conjecture for q-Catalan germs

reason: Sharp coefficient one and simultaneous part-count control require global connectivity partition surgery. Checking complete graphs or small k does not address arbitrary n,k.
source_name: Michitaka Furuya, Masaki Kashima and Katsuhiro Ota, “New Invariants for Partitioning a Graph into 2-connected Subgraphs”, arXiv:2403.08465 (2024).
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$, and let $k$ be an integer at least $2$. A partition $\mathcal{P}$ of $V(G)$ is **$k$-proper** if every part $P\in\mathcal{P}$ induces a $k$-connected subgraph of $G$, where a graph is $k$-connected if it has more than $k$ vertices and deleting any set of fewer than $k$ vertices leaves it connected. Write $\delta(G)$ for the minimum degree of $G$. **Borozan et al.'s conjecture.** If

$$
\delta(G)\geq\sqrt{(k-1)n},
$$

then $G$ has a $k$-proper partition $\mathcal{P}$ satisfying

$$
|\mathcal{P}|\leq\frac{n-k+1}{\delta(G)-k+2}.
$$

This would improve the known bound with constant $c=\frac{2123}{180}$ in the corresponding minimum-degree theorem, reducing that constant to $1$ and sharpening the bound on the number of parts.
title: Borozan et al.'s conjecture on k-proper partitions

reason: Only six dimensions but arbitrary lattices remain unbounded objects. Requires a universal Gram/lattice obstruction, not a catalogue of classical lattices; no finite certificate reduction.
source_name: Jacques Martinet, “Families of Equiangular Lines and Lattices”, arXiv:2403.09446 (2024).
statement:
Let $t'_n$ denote the largest number of lines in an equiangular family obtained from the minimal vectors of a lattice in dimension $n$. **Dimension $8$–$13$ conjecture.** For $8\le n\le 13$ we have

$$
t'_n\le 2n,
$$

and $t'_{13}=26$. This is motivated by lower bounds $t'_n\ge 2(n-1)$ and computational experiments with classical lattices of minimum $4$; the source gives no resolution of the conjecture.
title: The upper-bound conjecture for equiangular lines in dimensions 8 through 13

reason: Four dimensions do not bound lattice possibilities. Matching examples alone cannot prove optimality over all lattices; no universal upper-bound route.
source_name: Jacques Martinet, “Families of Equiangular Lines and Lattices”, arXiv:2403.09446 (2024).
statement: For a lattice in dimension $n$, consider the equiangular lines produced by its minimal vectors. **Minimal-vector line-count conjecture.** For $n=16$, $18$, $19$ and $20$, the largest number of such lines is $38$, $56$, $72$ and $90$, respectively. The conjecture concerns dimensions where the preceding table records matching known upper values and lattice constructions; the source gives no resolution beyond those computational comparisons.
title: The maximal-line conjecture for minimal vectors in dimensions 16, 18, 19 and 20

reason: Z^n gives ratio identically one, exposing argmin uniqueness wording only. Functional-equation symmetry does not prove a minimum for arbitrary unimodular lattices; no substantive full route.
source_name: Maiara F. Bollauf and Hsuan-Yin Lin, “On the Maximum Flatness Factor over Unimodular Lattices”, arXiv:2403.16932 (2025).
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a unimodular lattice, let $\Theta_{\Lambda}$ denote its theta series, and define

$$
\Delta_{\Lambda}(\tau)=\frac{\Theta_{\Lambda}(i\tau)}{\Theta_{\mathbb{Z}^n}(i\tau)}.
$$

**Global-minimum conjecture.** The theta series ratio achieves its global minimum at $\tau=1$:

$$
\operatorname*{argmin}_{\tau>0}\Delta_{\Lambda}(\tau)=1.
$$

The claim is related to the symmetry point at $\tau=1$ for unimodular lattices and would give the lower bound $\Delta_{\Lambda}(\tau)\geq\Delta_{\Lambda}(1)$ for all $\tau>0$. The source reports substantial supporting evidence but does not state that the conjecture has been resolved.
title: Global minimum conjecture for the theta series ratio of unimodular lattices

reason: Linear bounds do not give existence of D(n)/n limit. No near-superadditivity or composition theorem preserving the Waiter strategy.
source_name: Grzegorz Adamski, Sylwia Antoniuk, Małgorzata Bednarska-Bzdęga, Dennis Clemens, Fabian Hamann and Yannick Mogge, “Creating spanning trees in Waiter-Client games”, arXiv:2403.18534 (2024).
statement:
Let $D(n)$ be the largest integer $t$ such that for every tree $T$ with $v(T)=n$ and $Delta(T)\leq t$, Waiter has a winning strategy in $\operatorname{WC}(n,T)$. **Linear asymptotics conjecture.** There exists a constant $c$ such that

$$
D(n)=cn+o(n).
$$

The paper establishes linear lower and upper bounds on $D(n)$ that differ by a multiplicative constant; the conjecture asserts that a limiting linear constant exists.
title: Linear asymptotics conjecture for the Waiter-Client tree degree threshold

reason: Arbitrary tight forms may lack regularity and attained maxima on noncompact closure. Smooth-case principles cannot bridge weak regularity; wording corrections excluded.
source_name: Aidan Backus, “An -Laplacian for differential forms, and calibrated laminations”, arXiv:2404.02215 (2024).
statement:
Let $F$ be a tight form and let $U$ be an open set such that

$$
H_{d-1}(U,\mathbf{R})=0.
$$

**Absolute maximum principle for tight forms.** The restriction of $|F|$ to $\overline{U}$ attains its maximum on $\partial U$.
This would extend the absolute-minimization theorem from sufficiently regular tight forms to arbitrary tight forms; the authors state that they cannot prove it because they lack a maximum principle.
title: Absolute maximum principle for tight forms

reason: All dimensions and lattice polytopes require integer decomposition for every r. Edge length alone does not supply a triangulation with a controlled normality certificate; no bounded full route.
source_name: Lei Song, Huanqi Wen and Zhixian Zhu, “On Covering Simplices by Dilations in Dimensions 3 and 4”, arXiv:2404.02495 (2026).
statement:
Let $M$ be a lattice and let $P\subset M_{\mathbb{R}}$ be a lattice polytope of dimension $n$. Define the **lattice length** $l(P)$ to be the minimum, over all edges of $P$, of the number of lattice points on the edge minus one. **Song–Zhu conjecture.** If $l(P)\ge n-1$, then

$$
(rP\cap M)+(P\cap M)=(r+1)P\cap M
$$

for all $r\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$; equivalently, $P$ is integrally closed. The conjecture proposes a sufficient lattice-length condition for integral closure, extending known results in low dimensions and for sufficiently large $r$; its general validity remains open.
title: Song–Zhu conjecture on integral closure of lattice polytopes

reason: Uniform constant c with linear m threshold needs remove quadratic dependence on n,p in size-Ramsey extremal arguments. No matching universal lower/upper construction.
source_name: Fanghua Guo, Yanbo Zhang and Yunqing Zhang, “Matching-star size Ramsey numbers under connectivity constraint”, arXiv:2404.03175 (2024).
statement:
Let $nK_{1,p}$ be the disjoint union of $n$ copies of the star $K_{1,p}$, and let $K_{1,m}$ be the star with $m$ edges. The connected size Ramsey number $\hat r_c(G_1,G_2)$ is the minimum number of edges in a connected graph $G$ such that $G\to (G_1,G_2)$. **Linear-threshold conjecture.** There exists a positive constant $c$ such that for all positive integers $m$, $n$, and $p$ with $m\geq c(n+p)$, we have

$$
\hat r_c(nK_{1,p},K_{1,m})=n(m+p)-1.
$$

The conjecture proposes that the exact value established in the paper for the stronger condition $m\geq (n^2+2pn+n-3)/2$ remains valid once $m$ is merely linear in $n+p$.
title: Linear-threshold conjecture for connected size Ramsey numbers of star matchings

reason: All trees with arbitrary degrees require a uniform spectral-gap constant at every fugacity below e-1. Reconstruction intuition does not give a Poincaré inequality; no full mechanism.
source_name: Xiaoyu Chen, Xiongxin Yang, Yitong Yin and Xinyuan Zhang, “Spectral Independence Beyond Total Influence on Trees and Related Graphs”, arXiv:2404.04668 (2024).
statement: Let $T$ be a tree with $n$ vertices, and let $\lambda$ be the fugacity of the hardcore model. The Glauber dynamics is the single-site Markov chain for this Gibbs distribution, and its spectral gap is the smallest nonzero eigenvalue of the chain's Laplacian. **The hardcore-model tree spectral-gap conjecture.** For any tree $T$ with $n$ vertices, the spectral gap of the Glauber dynamics for the hardcore model on $T$ with fugacity $\lambda<e-1$ is at least $\Omega(n^{-1})$. This is proposed from the reconstruction threshold: the source notes that the reconstruction threshold exceeds $e-1$, while rapid mixing is known for sufficiently small fugacity and polynomial lower bounds occur for sufficiently large fugacity. The conjectured threshold and the full arbitrary-tree statement remain open.
title: The hardcore-model tree spectral-gap conjecture

reason: Every sufficiently large admissible order and every fixed chromatic number requires resolvability plus exact chromatic control. Existing nonresolvable constructions are insufficient.
source_name: Andrea C. Burgess, Nicholas J. Cavenagh, Peter Danziger and David A. Pike, “Weak colourings of Kirkman triple systems”, arXiv:2404.06066 (2025).
statement:
Let a **Kirkman triple system** of order $v$ be a resolvable Steiner triple system on $v$ points, and let its chromatic number be the minimum number of colours in a colouring in which every triple receives at least two colours. The admissible orders satisfy $v\equiv 3\pmod{6}$.

**Eventual chromatic spectrum conjecture.** For every integer $\delta\geqslant 3$, there exists an integer $v_0$ such that whenever $v\geqslant v_0$ and $v\equiv 3\pmod{6}$, there is a $\delta$-chromatic Kirkman triple system of order $v$.

This conjecture is the Kirkman-triple-system analogue of the corresponding result known for Steiner triple systems. It would establish the eventual existence of every chromatic number at every admissible order, but remains open.
title: The eventual chromatic spectrum conjecture for Kirkman triple systems

reason: Triangle dijoin suggests rank-one augmentation, but lower bound requires exact tournament-minimum-rank conventions and source results. No universal rank certificate proved.
source_name: Natalie Behague, Tom Johnston, Natasha Morrison and Shannon Ogden, “A note on inverting the dijoin of oriented graphs”, arXiv:2404.10663 (2025).
statement:
Let $D$ be a tournament, and let $\overrightarrow{C_3}$ denote the directed cycle on three vertices. The **tournament minimum rank** $\operatorname{tmr}(D)$ is the invariant used in the source for tournaments. **Directed-triangle minimum-rank conjecture.** For every tournament $D$, 
$$
\operatorname{tmr}(D\rightarrow\overrightarrow{C_3})=\operatorname{tmr}(D)+1=\operatorname{tmr}(\overrightarrow{C_3}\rightarrow D).
$$
 This is proposed as a special case of the question whether tournament minimum rank is additive under dijoins, and would provide a starting point for that broader problem.
title: Tournament minimum-rank additivity for a directed triangle

reason: Strict asymptotic separation needs compatible ordinary upper and rectilinear lower bounds with different leading behaviour or enough lower-order slack. Finite n examples insufficient.
source_name: Ruy Fabila-Monroy, Rosna Paul, Jenifer Viafara-Chanchi and Alexandra Weinberger, “On the rectilinear crossing number of complete balanced multipartite graphs and layered graphs”, arXiv:2404.13155 (2025).
statement:
Let $K_n^4$ denote the complete balanced $4$-partite graph with $n$ vertices, and let $\operatorname{cr}(G)$ and $\overline{\operatorname{cr}}(G)$ denote respectively its ordinary and rectilinear crossing numbers. **4-partite separation conjecture.** There exists a natural number $n_0>9$ such that, for every $n\geq n_0$,

$$
\operatorname{cr}(K_n^4)<\overline{\operatorname{cr}}(K_n^4).
$$

The known values and upper bounds at $n=8,9$ motivate the conjecture that, eventually, straight-line drawings require strictly more crossings than unrestricted drawings. The source does not determine such an $n_0$.
title: Strict crossing-number separation for balanced complete 4-partite graphs

reason: Statement explicitly reports public counterexamples. Do not count independent refutation; exact counterexample bodies not inspected here, so retain source confirmation HOLD rather than assert audited resolution.
source_name: Haozhe Wang, Yuxuan Yang and Mei Lu, “The inversion number of dijoins and blow-up digraphs”, arXiv:2404.14937 (2024).
statement:
For digraphs without loops, parallel edges, or $2$-cycles, let $L$ and $R$ be oriented graphs. The **dijoin** $L\Rightarrow R$ is formed from their disjoint union by adding an arc $uv$ for every $u\in V(L)$ and $v\in V(R)$. The inversion number $\operatorname{inv}(D)$ is the minimum size of a family of vertex subsets whose successive inversions make $D$ acyclic.

**Bang-Jensen et al.'s dijoin conjecture.** For oriented graphs $L$ and $R$,

$$
\operatorname{inv}(L\Rightarrow R)=\operatorname{inv}(L)+\operatorname{inv}(R).
$$

The conjecture is trivial when one of the two inversion numbers is zero and is known when their sum is at most $3$, as well as when both are $2$. It is false in general: counterexamples were independently found by Alon et al. and Aubian et al.
title: Bang-Jensen et al.'s dijoin conjecture for inversion number

reason: Three fixed rectangles needs a complete NP-hardness gadget reduction while retaining simply connected regions. A 111-tile reduction does not supply this; large formal/reduction burden.
source_name: Chao Yang and Zhujun Zhang, “NP-completeness of Tiling Finite Simply Connected Regions with a Fixed Set of Wang Tiles”, arXiv:2405.01017 (2024).
statement: A **rectangle tiling set** is a finite set $R$ of rectangles, and a simply connected region is a region in the plane without holes that is to be tiled using translated copies of rectangles from $R$. **Pak–Yang's conjecture.** There exists a set $R$ of $3$ rectangles such that tiling simply connected regions with $R$ is \textsf{NP}-complete. This conjecture concerns the minimum size of a fixed rectangle set yielding computationally intractable tiling; the paper proves the corresponding result for a set of $111$ rectangles, while the three-rectangle case remains open.
title: Pak–Yang's three-rectangle NP-completeness conjecture

reason: Sparsity definition not local, and quantifiers for every H,c demand a uniform sparse-host theorem. Ordinary induced-subdivision existence does not yield the claimed extremal count.
source_name: Jacob Fox, Rajko Nenadov and Huy Tuan Pham, “The largest subgraph without a forbidden induced subgraph”, arXiv:2405.05902 (2024).
statement:
Let $H$ be a graph, and let $\mathcal{D}_H$ be the property of not containing a subdivision of $H$ as an induced subgraph. For a graph $\Gamma$, write $\mathrm{ex}(\Gamma,\mathcal{D}_H)$ for the maximum number of edges in a subgraph of $\Gamma$ with this property. For $c>0$, say that $\Gamma$ is **$(c,t)$-sparse** when it satisfies the sparsity condition used in the paper. **Sparse-host induced subdivision extremal conjecture.** For every $c>0$ and a graph $H$, there exists $C>1$ such that, if $\Gamma$ is a $(c,t)$-sparse graph, then

$$
\mathrm{ex}(\Gamma,\mathcal{D}_H)\le Ctn.
$$

The motivation is a result showing that sufficiently dense graphs with no $K_{t,t}$ contain an induced subdivision of $H$; the stated sparse-host extremal estimate remains open.
title: Sparse-host induced subdivision extremal conjecture

reason: Every genus except two needs explicit near-triangular embeddings attaining a crossing lower bound. Sporadic genus constructions cannot establish the family; no uniform surgery route.
source_name: Timothy Sun, “On Kainen's conjectures on surface crossing numbers”, arXiv:2405.06118 (2024).
statement:
For each nonnegative integer $g\neq 2$, let

$$
M(g):=\left\lceil\frac{7+\sqrt{1+48g}}{2}\right\rceil
$$

and let $S_g$ denote the orientable surface of genus $g$. A **Kainen drawing** is a drawing attaining Kainen's lower bound for the surface crossing number. **Kainen's arbitrary-surface conjecture.** For each nonnegative integer $g\neq 2$, there exists a Kainen drawing of the complete graph $K_{M(g)}$ in $S_g$. This proposed common generalization of the paper's theorem and the minimum-triangulation result remains a belief stated in the conclusion; no resolution is supplied in the provided text.
title: Kainen's conjecture for complete graphs in arbitrary surfaces

primary_review.assessment: Conjecture 4.2 includes alpha=0; preceding Example 4.1 expressly calls alpha=0,p=1,q=0 and alpha=0,p=-1,q=1 known stabilization equalities. Proposition 1.5 gives L0=logarithmic mean. Thus endpoint repair is already acknowledged, not a substantive refutation. Off-diagonal alpha nonzero inequality remains unresolved here; asymptotic coefficient is only local evidence. Related accepted outcome35 concerns another mean, not a resolution of this alpha-family.

Thus endpoint repair is already acknowledged, not a substantive refutation. Off-diagonal alpha nonzero inequality remains unresolved here; asymptotic coefficient is only local evidence. Related accepted outcome35 concerns another mean, not a resolution of this alpha-family.
source_name: Lenka Mihoković and Mustapha Raïssouli, “Results on comparison and sub/super-stabilizability of some new means”, arXiv:2405.13618 (2024).
statement:
Let $L_\alpha$ denote the Stolarsky mean, let $B_p$ and $B_q$ be power means, and let $\mathcal{R}(B_p,L_\alpha,B_q)$ denote their associated stabilizing mean. Set

$$
q=\frac12(1-p)-2\alpha^2,\qquad p=\pm\sqrt{1+16\alpha^2-16\alpha^4}.
$$

**Sign conjecture.** The inequality

$$
L_\alpha-\mathcal{R}(B_p,L_\alpha,B_q)<0
$$

holds for $\lvert\alpha\rvert<\frac12$.

This statement concerns the sign needed to determine sub- or super-stabilizability of $L_\alpha$ by power means. The source presents it as motivated by numerical experiments; its resolution is not supplied.
title: Conjecture on the sign of the Stolarsky and power-mean difference

reason: Random residual after maximum clique packing needs dependencies controlled at an error o(sqrt(mu_r)). Existing r=3 argument or finite simulation is not the all-r structural theorem.
source_name: Zhifei Yan, “The chromatic number of very dense random graphs”, arXiv:2405.13914 (2024).
statement:
Fix $r\geqslant 4$, and let $G\sim G(n,q)$, where

$$
n^{-2/(r-1)}(\log n)^{1/{r-1 \choose 2}}\ll q=q(n)\ll n^{-2/r}.
$$

For each $r\in\mathbb{N}$, let $S_r(G)$ be the set of vertices in a largest $K_r$-matching of $G$, with an arbitrary deterministic choice in case of ties.

**Structural matching conjecture.** With high probability as $n\rightarrow\infty$, the graph $G-S_r(G)$ contains a $K_{r-1}$-matching that covers all but $o(\sqrt{\mu_r})$ vertices of $V(G)\setminus S_r(G)$.

This conjecture would provide the structural theorem needed to extend the paper's results to larger values of $r$. The source notes that the analogous case $r=3$ follows from an earlier structural result, while the cases $r\geqslant4$ remain open.
title: Structural matching conjecture for dense random graphs
